reason: The cited evidence shows DSC can measure melting enthalpy in a HEA (E1) and that melting point can be identified from enthalpy slope changes (E3), but it provides no support for the simultaneous DSC-XRD coupling, volume change measurement, or entropy derivation from integrated cp curves, which are central to the proposed method.
premises: DSC can resolve melting endotherms and enthalpy of fusion in HEAs
In-situ synchrotron XRD can track lattice parameter changes through melting
Simultaneous DSC-XRD allows direct calculation of volume change at melting
Configurational entropy can be derived from measured heat capacity curves
Melting temperature can be determined from the onset of the DSC endotherm or enthalpy slope change
